title: Annotatio IV §.XIII open: Ninth century — reclaimers against both Transubstantiations; Charlemagne FIGURE
pass_a_gloss: §. XIII. Although indeed from this point all the way to the most perverse times of the Reformation the Nicaeans’ Sentence — both concerning the Transmutation of the incorruptible God into the Image of corruptible man and concerning that of the Eucharistic bread into the Substance of Christ’s Body, unwritten and even anti-written — held first place, to be disseminated far and wide; yet even in the NINTH AGE there were found here and there who for their part would cry out against both Transubstantiations. For around the very entrance of the Ninth Age, the divine Emperor CHARLES, rightly called the GREAT, just as he restrained the veneration and sacred use of images by the Frankfurt Council within certain limits at least in the year 794, so also concerning the Eucharist he expressed the form of Christ’s sound words clearly enough in his Letter to Alcuin in these words: Dining, he says, with the Disciples, Christ broke bread and likewise gave them the cup in the FIGURE of His body and blood, and exhibited to us a great Sacrament that would profit us.
pass_b_english: §.XIII: though Nicaean sentences on image-transmutation and bread-into-Body held first place until the Reformation, the NINTH age still found reclaimers against both Transubstantiations.

Around its entrance CHARLES THE GREAT restrained image-veneration (Frankfurt 794) and, to Alcuin, said Christ gave bread and cup in the FIGURE of His body and blood — a great Sacrament for our profit.
source_text: §. XIII. Etsi verò ab hoc, ad Reformationis usque tempora perversissima, Nicænorum tam de incorruptibilis Dei in Imaginem hominis corruptibilis, quàm de panis Eucharistici in Corporis Christi Substantiam Transmutatione agraphô quin antigraphô, Sententia primas tenuerit, longe lateque disseminanda; inventi tamen etiam SECULO NONO, hinc inde sunt, qui utrique Transsubstantiationi pro virili reclamarent. Enimverò circa ipsum Seculi Noni ingressum, divus Imperator CAROLUS, jure suô MAGNUS appellatus, sicuti imaginum venerationem usumque sacrum, per Francofurtense Concilium, intra certos saltem limites, coërcuit Anno 794.; ita de Eucharistia quoque sanorum Christi verborum formam, in Epistola sua ad Alcuinum, luculenter satis hisce expressit: Cœnando, inquit, cum Discipulis Christus, panem fregit & calicem pariter dedit iis in FIGURAM corporis & sanguinis sui, nobisque profuturum magnum exhibuit Sacramentum.
